Start the Matrix Prior of a Random Effect at the Scale of the Data

Source: R/objective.R
statmod_hyper_scale_start.Rd

Moves the starting free values of every estimated matrix parameter (a covariance, precision or scale matrix carried by a parameters7 chart) so that the matrix describes effects whose variance is half the variance of the equation's working response at the intercept-only fit. The pattern of the matrix at the neutral start (the correlations, which are zero there) is kept, and only its scale changes.

Usage

statmod_hyper_scale_start(spec, design, hyper)

Arguments

spec

A StatmodSpec().

design

The design, as statmod_design() returns it.

hyper

The hyperparameters as statmod_hyper_start() returns them.

Value

hyper, with the free values of each matrix parameter moved.

Details

The neutral start of a chart is the identity matrix, a variance of one on the link scale. On a response measured in thousands that is a prior under which the effects are negligible, the marginal criterion is flat in the scale there, and an outer search started there can leave along a ridge instead of reaching the interior optimum.

The working response of equation \(p\) is \(z_i = \eta_p + U_{ip} / I_{ip}\), with \(U_{ip}\) the score and \(I_{ip}\) the expected information of observation \(i\) on the link scale, both at the intercept-only fit of statmod_intercepts(). For a gaussian location on the identity link it is the response itself. Half its weighted variance \(v\) is given to the effects: the target matrix is \(c M_0\) for a covariance or a scale matrix and \(M_0 / c\) for a precision, with \(M_0\) the matrix at the neutral start and \(c\) chosen so that the mean variance of the effects is \(v\). The free values are parameters7::param_free() of that target.

A matrix parameter is left at its neutral start when any of its free values is held, when the unit belongs to a structural term or to a covariance class, when the response is multivariate, and when any step above fails or returns a value that is not finite.

See also

statmod_hyper_start(), which supplies the neutral start.
